In scenario 2, the swimmer holds the same block at rest in a tank of salt water where density rho 2 is bigger than rho 1.
The swimmer again releases the block from rest and the block accelerates upwards with an initial acceleration a2. All frictional forces are negligible.

The force for buoyancy is rho vg, where rho is the density of the fluid, v is the volume displaced, and g is the acceleration due to gravity, and fg is simply just mass times gravity over m.
And I would just factor out g, so g times rho v minus m over m, and that would be your net acceleration initially.
